findings.summary: The dependents list omits the per-wave re-plan, which is now the only thing holding back items that depend on the passed-over item.
findings.evidence: Before, Failed stopped the run (finish 2379), so a dependent never ran. With Paused the loop goes on, and drain_with calls prepare again before the next wave. prepare holds back every item that depends on a paused id. The plan names neither this path nor a test for it, and the new test's items have no dependency. Fix: Add a dependents entry for the per-wave re-plan, and a test where c depends on a: after a's second failure pauses its line, c is not read or run and gets a 'depends on a, which is held back' passed-over line, b lands, and the stop is not RepeatedFailure.

findings.summary: The new test's Stub sets no plan entries.
findings.evidence: With no entries, items are worked one at a time in queue order (batches_for 2701-2711). The existing paused-line tests (tests/drain.rs 596-641) use plan entries. Fix: Add planned(...) entries, so the test also covers the planned path and can carry the dependency case.

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG risk points to the wrong step number.
findings.evidence: The risk says step 5; the CHANGELOG step is step 6. Fix: Change it to step 6.

summary: I checked the plan against the code by reading it. Everything it names exists as described. Drain::attempts already checks the pause at the top of each attempt (drain.rs 1745-1752), and it returns Failed at the second failure (1811-1814) without checking again. finish turns Failed into Stop::RepeatedFailure (2379) and Paused into a passed-over line (2413). The Stub keys pauses by item id. The real Steps::paused reloads records on every call (3243, 3326). Checking once more where the failure is decided fixes the fault where it starts, and the new test drives the real drain::drain through the Steps seam and would fail without the fix. The one gap: before this change the batch stopped at the second failure, so items depending on that item never ran. Now only the per-wave re-plan holds them back (drain_with 2832-2837 calls prepare, which holds dependents at 2041-2064). The plan does not list that path and no test covers it.
